memories.author: D01
memories.text: Allergy: penicillin, anaphylaxis (throat swelling and low blood pressure) after an amoxicillin injection in 2019. Reaction was immediate and severe. Recorded 2025-04-22 by Dr Anjali Mehta (D01); patient advised to tell every prescriber and pharmacist.

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o asthma. c/o cough and chest tightness at night x 2 wks, worse in dusty weather. Salbutamol SOS used 3 times this week. No fever.
O: BP 122/78 mmHg, pulse 84/min, SpO2 98% RA. Chest: scattered wheeze on forced expiry, air entry good.
A: 1. Asthma, mild; reliever only for now. 2. Allergy history updated.
P: 1. Salbutamol (Asthalin) 100 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs SOS for breathlessness or wheeze. 2. Avoid dust, smoke and cold air where possible. 3. Home peak flow chart to be kept.
Adv: Warm up before exercise, walk 30 min daily, carry the inhaler at all times. R/V in 6 months.

memories.author: D01
memories.text: Rx change: START salbutamol (Asthalin) 100 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs as needed (SOS) for wheeze or breathlessness. Effective 2025-04-22. See doctor if needed more often than usual.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: App message from patient, 2025-06-18: 'Doctor, my chest feels tight when I cycle to the office in the rain and the cold air in the mornings. Should I use my blue inhaler before the ride? I have used it about twice this week.'

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o asthma. c/o night-time cough and wheeze on 3 nights a week for last 4 weeks. Salbutamol SOS 4 times a week. Audit season started, long hours indoors.
O: BP 124/80 mmHg, pulse 80/min, SpO2 97% RA. Chest: bilateral scattered wheeze, air entry good.
A: 1. Asthma, not controlled on reliever alone; step-up needed.
P: 1. Start budesonide-formoterol (Foracort) 200/6 inhaler, 1 puff BD, regular, even when well. 2. Cont salbutamol (Asthalin) SOS. 3. Inhaler technique checked and demonstrated. 4. Rinse mouth after each budesonide-formoterol dose.
Adv: Avoid smoke and dust, 30 min walk daily, regular sleep. R/V in 3 months.

memories.author: D01
memories.text: Rx change: START budesonide-formoterol (Foracort) 200/6 inhaler, 1 puff twice daily (morning and night), regular use. Effective 2025-09-16. Salbutamol (Asthalin) 100 mcg SOS continues unchanged.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: App message from patient, 2025-10-02: 'Doctor, I started the twice-daily inhaler last week. My nights are much better and I have not needed the blue inhaler at night. Can I stop it once I feel fine?'

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o asthma. Night symptoms settled since starting the regular inhaler. Salbutamol used once in the past 3 months. Missed the evening dose occasionally.
O: BP 126/80 mmHg, pulse 76/min, SpO2 99% RA. Chest clear.
A: 1. Asthma, well controlled on budesonide-formoterol.
P: 1. Cont budesonide-formoterol (Foracort) 200/6, 1 puff BD. 2. Cont salbutamol (Asthalin) SOS. 3. Explained that the regular inhaler must not be stopped when well. 4. Technique checked, good.
Adv: Keep to the inhaler routine, avoid smoke, walk 30 min 5 days a week. R/V in 6 months.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: App message from patient, 2026-01-22: 'Doctor, I caught a cold last week. My chest was tight for two nights and the blue inhaler helped. The regular inhaler is working, but I still get a little cough in the mornings. Should I come in to see you?'

memories.author: patient
memories.text: App message from patient, 2026-04-09: 'Doctor, the pharmacy was out of my twice-daily inhaler for five days. I used the blue inhaler a little more during those days, maybe 3 times. I have restarted the regular one now.'

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o asthma. Feels well, no night symptoms. Salbutamol about once a month. Restarted the regular inhaler after the pharmacy shortage in April.
O: BP 120/78 mmHg, pulse 74/min, SpO2 98% RA. Chest clear. Inhaler technique good.
A: 1. Asthma, well controlled.
P: 1. Cont budesonide-formoterol (Foracort) 200/6, 1 puff BD. 2. Cont salbutamol (Asthalin) SOS. 3. Refill the regular inhaler before it runs out.
Adv: Avoid smoke and dust, walk 30 min daily, keep the inhaler handy. R/V in 6 months.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: App message from patient, 2026-08-27: 'Doctor, I am a chartered accountant and audit season has been brutal. I missed my evening puffer about 3 or 4 times this month. I have been OK, just a little cough on some mornings. What is the best way to remember it?'

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o asthma. c/o sore throat and fever x 2 days, body ache, mild cough. Pain on swallowing. No breathlessness, no wheeze.
O: Temp 38.6°C, pulse 102/min, BP 118/76 mmHg, SpO2 98% RA. O/E: pharynx congested; tonsils enlarged with exudate; tender anterior cervical nodes. Chest clear.
A: 1. Sore throat with fever and tonsillar exudate, ? streptococcal; RADT sent. 2. Asthma, stable.
P: 1. Rapid strep test (RADT) sent today; result awaited. 2. Decide on antibiotic after the RADT result. 3. Warm fluids, salt water gargles, rest. 4. Cont budesonide-formoterol (Foracort) 200/6 BD and salbutamol (Asthalin) SOS.
Adv: Warm fluids, rest at home, avoid cold drinks, keep away from crowded places for now. R/V in 1 wk.
